title: Descent of one stabilizer component
statement: Let R and H be commutative rings, g in R, and ι:R→H. Let C be a domain H-algebra finite and faithfully flat over H. A finite group G acts on C by H-algebra maps ρ, preserving identity and multiplication. Assume h=algebraMap H C (ι(g)) is nonzero, D(h)→Spec H is etale, and any two field-valued points of C over H on which h is nonzero differ by a unique ρ(ζ). Let p:Y→Spec R factor through a finite etale j:Y→D(g). Given t:T→Spec R, k:D(h)→T over Spec R, and a splitting δ:Y×T≅∐(Fin d) T over T, use the explicit label action A of [lem-sbc-affine-torsor-split-label-laws]. Let x∈Fin d and K≤G be exactly its stabilizer under A. Put F=⋂ζ∈K Eq(ρ(ζ),id) as an H-subalgebra of C, U=D(algebraMap H F (ι(g))) in Spec F, and q:D(h)→U the restriction of Spec(F→C). There exists an open immersion f:U→Y×Spec H whose projection to Spec H is the natural U→Spec H, and such that q followed by f and projection to Y equals the x-th split section pulled back along k.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite Galois covers and permutation sets; stabilizer quotient argument

proof.text:
localize at h = algebraMap H C (ι g). Finite faithful flatness and
etaleness give a connected finite etale cover of D(ι g); unique rotations make it
Galois with deck group G. Pull delta back along k. Connectedness makes the deck
permutation on sections equal to its label at the zero prime. The exact stabilizer
of the chosen label is K, so the associated transitive subcover is V/K and its map
into the original cover is an open-and-closed immersion. The affine quotient ring
is C[1/h]^K. It equals (C^K)[1/h]: an invariant fraction a/h^n has invariant numerator,
because h is fixed and localization of the domain C is injective. Conversely an
invariant numerator gives an invariant fraction. Under the basic-open localization
identification the quotient map is the restriction q of Spec(F -> C). Descending
the chosen section gives f, with q followed by f and projection to Y equal to that
section. All quotient maps are over Spec H, giving the projection equation.
No completeness or distinctness of a family of representatives is used.

proof_origin.note: Isolated part of orbit-component descent; not a restatement of the coproduct isomorphism.
